title: [Draft] Experimental Dynamic GI improvements

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? Implements software-traced, high-quality real-time global illumination based on HDDAGI (awesome work originally posted by [reduz](https://github.com/reduz) in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/86267 and later rebased by [OrangeeZ](https://github.com/OrangeeZ) in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119869). This draft PR is totally not ready for review or merge right now, but is mainly for testing and discussion purposes. It's too much loc and should be separated into several smaller PRs if there's a chance to merge them. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8c1c84d-1fa5-4e8c-b03a-31bcbf0d343f I started working on it for our WIP game project. As quite a lot of people asked about it, I spent some time taking it out of our private branch. To be honest, the implementation is a bit heuristic and a mixture of different approaches, mainly inspired by [Kajiya](https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/kajiya) and Unreal's Lumen. I'm not quite sure if this can run well on potato machines finally, but performance will still be the next things I'll working on. Users have no reason running this with lower quality and performance on an extreme GPU that usually supports hardware accelarated RT lol. ## Progress in this PR right now - ported/rebased the original HDDAGI implementation to the current rendering architecture and octahedral sky radiance layout, while preserving SDFGI compatibility - screen-probe diffuse indirect lighting in two modes - Stochastic Integrated probes - Lumen-style Directional Gather probes with adaptive 8 × 8 directional sampling - optional guided/importance sampling for both screen-probe modes - optional screen-space detail tracing for near-field geometry and visible dynamic surfaces - an optional SVGF denoiser for diffuse lighting and reflections (BTW, NVIDIA NRD was removed from this PR to keep it simple and clean) - optional GGX-based screen-traced HDDAGI reflections (WIP, basically works but needs more tweaks) - an optional irradiance cache with an experimental multi-bounce path, to replace the original recursive bounce feedback (WIP, not really necessary and needs more tweaks, might be removed if I found any way to make HDDA's bounce more accurate) - optional camera-local anchor and forward-offset controls for HDDAGI cascades (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12293) - stable skinned-mesh motion-vector history for temporal screen-probe filtering - HDDAGI area light support - a 3 × 3 screen-probe debug montage ## Known issues - screen-probe reflections can be kind of noisy and laggy on some surfaces. - the irradiance cache can flicker and is currently only supported by Stochastic Integrated mode, so you'd better leave it disabled for now. - adaptive directional probes need more tweaks; the subdivided probe pool can easily reach its limit. - performance is not well tuned yet. It is a good idea to use FSR upscaling or half-resolution GI. - ~~you might notice that half-resolution GI does not improve performance much in Directional Gather mode for now.~~ Solved in the newest commit. - indirect lighting can still be unstable in some really hard-to-sample places. - ~~bad hdda voxels on thin plates/corners still leads to noticable artifacts~~ Partially solved by jittering probes. - tested on Windows(Vulkan/D3D12), MacOS(Metal), Android(Vulkan Forward+). ## If someone wanna give a try... Set the denoiser to SVGF(sorry that I didn't make it the default option) ~~and toggle on detail trace and guided sampling~~ **UPDATE**: hiz detail tracing can lead to extra perf cost on lower end devices, now with probes jittering we could handle corners well without detail tracing. Then in the Environment - Dynamic GI, toggle on screen probes. As for mode, Stochastic Integration has better details and deals with corners better, while Directional Gather usually runs 20%~40% faster. **UPDATE**: It's more recommanded to use GI half resolution with Directional Gather Mode. This could usually be a sweet point for both performance and quality. ## Some results Other other old screenshots can be found in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119869#issuecomment-5386916094 Left-HDDA GI basic vs Right-HDDAGI with Screen Probes Official TPS Demo Running on MacBook Air M2
